ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, in $\triangle ABC$, $AB=AC$, the perpendicular bisector $MN$ of $AB$ intersects $AC$ at point $D$ and intersects $AB$ at point $E$, $\angle A=36^\circ$, $AD=5$, find the degree measure of $\angle DBC$ and the length of side $BC$.
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Since in $\triangle ABC$, $AB=AC$ and $\angle A=36^\circ$,\\
it follows that $\angle ABC=\angle C=\frac{180^\circ-\angle A}{2}=72^\circ$,\\
Since the perpendicular bisector of $AB$, $MN$, intersects $AC$ at point $D$,\\
it follows that $AD=BD$,\\
Therefore, $\angle ABD=\angle A=36^\circ$,\\
Therefore, $\angle DBC=\angle ABC-\angle ABD=36^\circ$,\\
Since $\angle BDC=\angle ABD+\angle A=72^\circ$,\\
it follows that $\angle BDC=\angle C=72^\circ$,\\
Therefore, $BC=BD$,\\
Also, since $AD=BD$,\\
it follows that $BC=AD=\boxed{5}$.

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The diagram shows triangle ABC with A at the top apex, B at the lower left, and C at the lower right. Point D is on side AC, point E is on side AB, a slanted line MN passes through E and D, and segment BD is drawn inside the triangle. Reasoning: Since AB=AC and ∠A=36°, triangle ABC is isosceles with base angles ∠ABC=∠ACB=(180°−36°)/2=72°. Since MN is the perpendicular bisector of AB and D lies on MN, D is equidistant from A and B, so AD=BD. Given AD=5, we have BD=5. In triangle ABD, AD=BD, so the base angles at A and B are equal; because ∠DAB=∠A=36°, ∠ABD=36°. Therefore ∠DBC=∠ABC−∠ABD=72°−36°=36°. Since D lies on AC, ∠BDC is the exterior angle of triangle ABD at D, so ∠BDC=∠DAB+∠ABD=36°+36°=72°. In triangle DBC, ∠DCB=∠ACB=72° and ∠BDC=72°, so the opposite sides are equal: BC=BD. Hence BC=BD=AD=5.
